A deploy needs the values, not only the keys, and the two commands that write a
file needed a say in where it lands.

### Added

- `poo @profile --WITH_SECRETS` writes each key as a vault lookup rather than a
  bare name:

  ```sh
  monkeys poo @production --WITH_SECRETS
  ```
  ```
  # monkeys' poo @production, vault lookups. read https://monk3ys.dev/poo
  DATABASE_URL="$(security find-generic-password -s monkeys -a shop.production/DATABASE_URL -w)"
  PORT=8080
  ```

  That is the line `export` already writes, so nothing of the secret is on
  disk and the file is as safe to keep as the keys were. A shell resolves it
  with `set -a; . ./.env; set +a`. The profile has to be named, since a lookup
  carries one profile's stored name and the wrong one resolves to the wrong
  secret rather than to nothing.

  `--EXPAND_DANGEROUSLY` writes the secrets themselves, in the open. It is the
  one command in `monkeys` that does, it shouts for a reason, and it is for the
  tool that cannot run a lookup.
- `--path DIR` on `poo` and on `pack` names the directory to write into, and
  `pack` takes a file name before `--only`. Anywhere inside a git checkout both
  ask first, because that is where a commit can find the file:

  > ```
  > a .env into ~/code/shop/.env, where a commit can take it. go ahead? [y/N]
  > ```

  A `.env` that `poo` did not write is left alone rather than overwritten.

### Changed

- `forget` and `drop` ask before a secret goes, since the vault is the only
  place that secret exists:

  > ```
  > forget foo.test/STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, which nothing else holds. go ahead? [y/N]
  > ```

  The question needs a terminal, so a script or an agent is refused rather than
  answered for.

### Fixed

- `monk3ys.dev/poo`, the address every `poo` file carries, went through a 308
  on the way to the page.

### Documentation

- Every page opens with a line saying what it is, every index is generated, and
  each kind of thing a command does has one verb across the docs.
